findings.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so the keys collide and the intended numeric-expiry validation does not exist, letting responses with missing/garbage expiry pass validation and be written to credential.key

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts injects the literal string "refresh_token" when the response has no refresh_token, and office365calendar CalendarService spreads and persists it, overwriting the user's real refresh token with a placeholder

refreshOAuthTokens.ts sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts does `res?.data`, so token is undefined and `token.access_token` throws, breaking Google Calendar token refresh when credential sharing is enabled
hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts casts the sync-mode fetch Response to HubspotToken, so `expires_in` is undefined and the computed expiryDate becomes NaN and is persisted

zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId`, so the sync endpoint receives a credential ID as calcomUserId and may resolve to a different user's credentials
zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts (and zoho-bigin) expects an axios response but the sync branch returns a fetch Response, so `zohCrmTokenInfo.data.error` dereferences undefined and throws a TypeError
salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 checks `response.statusText !== "OK"`, which is an empty string on HTTP/2 responses, causing successful refreshes to throw; should use `!response.ok`

salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts runs the token refresh unconditionally on every service construction with no expiry check, adding a token round-trip plus credential.update write per operation and risking Salesforce refresh-token rate limits

packages/lib/constants.ts:103 APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to the encryption key string rather than a boolean, so a constant named _ENABLED holds a secret that can be logged or leaked; should wrap in !!(...)
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts compares the webhook secret with `!==` instead of a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts reads `req.headers[...]` which may be `string | string[]`, so a duplicated header yields an array and the secret comparison silently fails

refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication or signature, allowing any party who can reach the endpoint to request an access token for an arbitrary calcomUserId, and nothing documents that self-hosters must authenticate it

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts uses `schema.parse(req.body)`, which throws on malformed input producing an unhandled rejection and a 500 with a Zod stack trace instead of a 400; should use safeParse

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts does not wrap symmetricDecrypt or JSON.parse in try/catch, so a wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext crashes the handler with a 500 and no actionable message

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts uses findFirst followed by create, a read-then-write race that lets concurrent webhook deliveries for the same (userId, appId) create duplicate credentials, with no unique constraint to catch it

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts ships with no tests despite being a new unauthenticated-by-default endpoint that writes decrypted OAuth credentials for arbitrary user IDs, and parseRefreshTokenResponse is likewise untested

office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts removed the console.error logging the Zod error and raw MS response, so parse failures now throw from parseRefreshTokenResponse with a generic message and no diagnostic context for Outlook refresh failures

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts throws on `!success`, making every caller's `if (!parsed.success)` / `parsed.success && parsed.data` branch (salesforce, zoomvideo, office365calendar) dead code implying a soft-failure path that no longer exists

zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 replaces `${appConfig.slug}` with a hardcoded "zoho-bigin", reintroducing drift between the route and config.json and likely leaving the appConfig import unused (lint/noUnusedLocals failure); the change is also unrelated to the PR's purpose

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts compares the webhook secret with `!==` instead of a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the webhook authentication check directly compares a secret from the request header to process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using `!==`. This is a normal string comparison and is not constant-time, so it can theoretically leak information about the secret via timing differences. A constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on normalized Buffers) is the typical mitigation when comparing secrets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts reads `req.headers[...]` which may be `string | string[]`, so a duplicated header yields an array and the secret comparison silently fails

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check compares `req.headers[headerName]` directly to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next.js/Node, `req.headers[...]` is typed and can be `string | string[] | undefined` when a header is repeated. If it’s an array, strict inequality against the expected secret string will always fail, causing legitimate requests with duplicated headers to be rejected (403). The code does not normalize/handle the `string[]` case.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the code does a POST fetch to the configured endpoint with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body and no authentication mechanism (no shared secret header, signature, token, etc.). The only guidance in-code is “Customize the payload…” and it does not document that the endpoint must enforce its own auth. This is a verifiable security/design gap introduced in the diff, especially contrasted with the separate webhook handler which does implement a shared-secret header check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts does not wrap symmetricDecrypt or JSON.parse in try/catch, so a wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext crashes the handler with a 500 and no actionable message

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the handler does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no try/catch. If CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing/wrong, or if symmetricDecrypt returns invalid/non-JSON plaintext, either symmetricDecrypt or JSON.parse can throw. That exception is not handled anywhere in the handler, so the Next.js API route will error out (500) instead of returning a controlled 4xx with an actionable message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts uses findFirst followed by create, a read-then-write race that lets concurrent webhook deliveries for the same (userId, appId) create duplicate credentials, with no unique constraint to catch it

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, it does a non-atomic read-then-write: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and if none is found it calls `prisma.credential.create(...)`. With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)`, both requests can observe “no credential” and both attempt `create`, which can result in duplicate rows (if the DB allows) or an unhandled create error (if a unique constraint exists). The diff itself does not show the Prisma schema, so the claim that there is "no unique constraint" is not directly verifiable from this diff, but the race/atomicity issue in this code path is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts ships with no tests despite being a new unauthenticated-by-default endpoint that writes decrypted OAuth credentials for arbitrary user IDs, and parseRefreshTokenResponse is likewise untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new API route (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) and new helpers (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) without adding any accompanying test files in this patch, but “ships with no tests” isn’t a verifiable defect from the diff alone (tests could already exist elsewhere or be added in another change). Also, the endpoint is not strictly “unauthenticated-by-default” in the code shown: it is gated by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and a shared-secret header check. While there may be configuration pitfalls (e.g., empty/undefined secrets), the proposed finding as written primarily asserts lack of tests and mischaracterizes the endpoint as unauthenticated-by-default, which is not strictly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts removed the console.error logging the Zod error and raw MS response, so parse failures now throw from parseRefreshTokenResponse with a generic message and no diagnostic context for Outlook refresh failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `console.error(...)` block in `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and replaces direct `safeParse` with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure. So it’s true that failures now have a more generic error and no longer log the Zod error/MS response. However, this is not clearly a defect introduced by the diff: removing logging of the raw Microsoft token response can be an intentional security/PII improvement (token responses can contain sensitive data), and switching from “log and continue” to “throw” is also plausibly an intentional correctness change rather than a bug. The finding frames this as a problem, but it’s primarily an observability preference and not an objectively verifiable bug/security/correctness issue on its own.
